knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Derivative of a Function of Three Intermediate Variables and Two Independent Variables

question.:question/problem: Let $f(x,y,z)=(-1)\cdot (y)+(2)\cdot (x)+(3)\cdot (z),$ where $x=t - 3 s$, $y=- t - 2 s$, $z=- s + 2 t$. Calculate $\frac{∂f}{∂s}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/be/be6afcdd0ad9ae0d7ef377c4918442a64e1186c90c25e27ec6c224d816a602fd.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y,z)$ with two independent variables $s$ and $t,$ where $x=x(s,t),y=y(s,t)$ and $z=z(s,t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂s}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\cdot \frac{∂z}{∂s}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x,y$ and $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=-1,\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ with respect to $s,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂s} & =-3, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂s} & =-2, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂s} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂s} & =(2)\cdot (-3)+(-1)\cdot (-2)+(3)\cdot (-1) \\  & =-6 + 2 - 3 \\  & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Let $f(x,y,z)=(-3)\cdot (x)+(3)\cdot (y)+(3)\cdot (z),$ where $x=s + t$, $y=- t + 2 s$, $z=- 3 s + 2 t$. Calculate $\frac{∂f}{∂s}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/be/be6afcdd0ad9ae0d7ef377c4918442a64e1186c90c25e27ec6c224d816a602fd.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y,z)$ with two independent variables $s$ and $t,$ where $x=x(s,t),y=y(s,t)$ and $z=z(s,t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂s}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\cdot \frac{∂z}{∂s}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x,y$ and $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=-3,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=3,\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}=3.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ with respect to $s,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂s} & =1, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂s} & =2, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂s} & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂s} & =(-3)\cdot (1)+(3)\cdot (2)+(3)\cdot (-3) \\  & =-3 + 6 - 9 \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Let $f(x,y,z)=(-1)\cdot (z)+(-2)\cdot (x)+(3)\cdot (y),$ where $x=t - 3 s$, $y=- s - t$, $z=- s + 2 t$. Calculate $\frac{∂f}{∂s}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/be/be6afcdd0ad9ae0d7ef377c4918442a64e1186c90c25e27ec6c224d816a602fd.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y,z)$ with two independent variables $s$ and $t,$ where $x=x(s,t),y=y(s,t)$ and $z=z(s,t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂s}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\cdot \frac{∂z}{∂s}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x,y$ and $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=-2,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=3,\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ with respect to $s,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂s} & =-3, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂s} & =-1, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂s} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂s} & =(-2)\cdot (-3)+(3)\cdot (-1)+(-1)\cdot (-1) \\  & =6 - 3 + 1 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Let $f(x,y,z)=(-1)\cdot (x)+(-1)\cdot (z)+(2)\cdot (y),$ where $x=t + 3 s$, $y=s - t$, $z=- 3 s + 2 t$. Calculate $\frac{∂f}{∂s}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/be/be6afcdd0ad9ae0d7ef377c4918442a64e1186c90c25e27ec6c224d816a602fd.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y,z)$ with two independent variables $s$ and $t,$ where $x=x(s,t),y=y(s,t)$ and $z=z(s,t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂s}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\cdot \frac{∂z}{∂s}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x,y$ and $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=-1,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2,\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}=-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ with respect to $s,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂s} & =3, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂s} & =1, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂s} & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂s} & =(-1)\cdot (3)+(2)\cdot (1)+(-1)\cdot (-3) \\  & =-3 + 2 + 3 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Let $f(x,y,z)=(-3)\cdot (y)+(-2)\cdot (x)+(-2)\cdot (z),$ where $x=t - 3 s$, $y=- t + 3 s$, $z=2 s + 2 t$. Calculate $\frac{∂f}{∂s}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
![](images/be/be6afcdd0ad9ae0d7ef377c4918442a64e1186c90c25e27ec6c224d816a602fd.png)

The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y,z)$ with two independent variables $s$ and $t,$ where $x=x(s,t),y=y(s,t)$ and $z=z(s,t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂s}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\cdot \frac{∂z}{∂s}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x,y$ and $z:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=-2,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=-3,\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ with respect to $s,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂s} & =-3, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂s} & =3, \\ \frac{∂z}{∂s} & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂s} & =(-2)\cdot (-3)+(-3)\cdot (3)+(-2)\cdot (2) \\  & =6 - 9 - 4 \\  & =-7.\end{aligned}
$$
